subject: KMS-split hosting acknowledgement and fallback runbook
messages:
From: Ari Patel <ari@novuslabs.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Cruz <elena.cruz@novuslabs.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Data residency confirmation + KMS split scenario

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We are preparing our security review for a potential Private deployment of Redwood in a dual-region configuration (US and EU). A couple items we need to resolve before procurement: 

- Can Redwood commit to a KMS split for customer-managed keys so that EU workloads use EU-managed CMKs and US workloads use US-managed CMKs?
- Where do backups and audit logs land by default (region and retention)? Can those be pinned to the same jurisdiction as the compute?
- If we failover from EU -> US for operational reasons, what is the documented fallback path and are there any cross-border key operations required?

We also need CAIQ/SIG slices that specifically call out VPC peering, PrivateLink endpoints, and key management separation. If you can provide an attestation or short runbook we can include with our SOC 2 package, that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Ari
Ari Patel
Head of Infrastructure, Novus Labs
ari@novuslabs.com
+1 415-555-0198

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ari Patel <ari@novuslabs.com>
Cc: Elena Cruz <elena.cruz@novuslabs.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Data residency confirmation + KMS split scenario

Hi Ari —

Appreciate the clear list. Short answers up front:

- Yes: we support customer-managed keys with region-bound CMKs and can map keys per region/tenant in Private deployments.
- Backups & audit logs: by default land in the deployment region and can be configured to retain in-region storage only; retention is configurable (30/90/365 days typical).
- Failover: we provide a documented fallback runbook; cross-border key usage is avoided by default — when an admin initiates cross-region failover we require a controlled key rotation/replicate step (described below).

Attaching a concise runbook and a checklist for PrivateLink + fallback flows. Rishi and Grace are cc'd to confirm technical nuance and provide a SIG/CAIQ mapping slice.

Next steps: please confirm the jurisdictional controls you require (e.g., "no cross-border backups", "EU-only logs", retention window) and we will produce a signed attestation and the CAIQ slice within 3 business days.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
(415) 555-0123

Attachments: redwood-kms-split-runbook.pdf (runbook stub), privatelink-fallback-checklist.xlsx (checklist stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 15:00:00 -0500
Subject: Fw: Data residency confirmation + KMS split scenario

Team — forwarding Novus' ask. High level: they want a KMS-per-region guarantee, in-region backups/logs, and a clear failover play that avoids implicit cross-border key usage.

Please: 
- Rishi, can you confirm the exact admin steps (and any required approvals) we gate on to perform a controlled cross-region failover? We should include CLI/API examples and required audit entries.
- Grace, can you prepare a CAIQ/SIG slice focusing on: PrivateLink configuration, VPC peering details, audit log residency, and the KMS split mapping? Aim for a 1–2 page runnable slice.
- Kimberly, once we have the attestation language, can you coordinate sign-off and get Legal to stamp it?

Feel free to use the attached runbook/checklist as a starting point. I want this back to me within the day so I can send Novus the attestation and CAIQ slice by EOD.

Thanks —
Marissa

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ari Patel <ari@novuslabs.com>
Cc: Elena Cruz <elena.cruz@novuslabs.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 16:20:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Data residency confirmation + KMS split scenario

Hi Ari —

Thanks for the patience. Attached are the two stubs we discussed and a short summary below; I’ve included the CAIQ/SIG slice link and draft attestation language for your review.

Summary (key points):
- KMS split: Redwood supports customer-managed CMKs scoped per-region. In a Private deployment we map tenant workloads to the CMK assigned to the deployment region. No cross-border key usage occurs unless the customer explicitly initiates a controlled failover.
- Backups & logs: created in-region by default and configurable to remain in-region for retention windows you choose. Audit trails record key access ops, replication events, and all administrative actions.
- Failover flow: documented three-step process — (1) Request & approve failover in Console (audit entry generated), (2) Execute controlled key-replicate operation (requires Security admin role; rotation keys are created in target region), (3) Confirm KV cache and replay point; validate integrity checks before switching traffic. See attached runbook for CLI samples.

CAIQ/SIG slice: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cDemoRunbook (CAIQ/controls slice 'Novus-privatelink-slice.pdf' in folder)

Draft attestation language (for your security pack):
"Redwood Inference confirms that, for Private deployments, customer data at rest (including backups and audit logs) is stored in the deployment region. Customer-managed keys are scoped per-region and no cross-border key operations are performed unless expressly authorized by the customer's Security Administrator via the documented failover procedure. Redwood can provide signed attestation upon mutual signature of the runbook and acceptance of the failover checklist."

Next steps: Please review the attachments and confirm any changes to the failover governance model you require (e.g., multi-signature approvals, change windows). Once you confirm, Kimberly will circulate a final signed attestation and the CAIQ/SIG slice within 48 hours.

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

(415) 555-0123
